newsitem.title: USA: MTV and Paramount buoy Viacom's profits.
newsitem.headline: MTV and Paramount buoy Viacom's profits.

text.p: Entertainment giant Viacom Inc. said Friday its profits rose in the third quarter, based on the strength of its MTV Networks, Paramount studios and Blockbuster video store results.
Paramount's profits were helped by the success of films such as "Mission Impossible," while MTV enjoyed strong gains in affiliate fees and advertising.
Viacom said its earnings rose to $102 million, or 27 cents a share, compared with $78 million, or 17 cents a share, in the year-earlier period.
Revenues in the third quarter rose to $3.35 billion from $2.95 billion a year earlier.
"At Blockbuster, we continue to generate strong revenue growth as we expand both domestically and in key territories abroad," Chairman Sumner Redstone said in a statement.

Separately, Blockbuster said it would move its headquarters to Dallas from Fort Lauderdale, Fla., next spring. All 1,000 employees in Fort Lauderdale will be offered jobs at the new location, as well as relocation support, it said.
Blockbuster currently employs nearly 1,200 people in the Dallas/Fort Worth area in retail stores and distribution centres.
"It makes good business sense to have all of our headquarters operations in the same city," Blockbuster Chief Executive Bill Fields said in a statement.
Redstone said the performance at MTV Networks was outstanding, with 27 percent gains in both revenues and earnings before income taxes, depreciation and other charges.
Paramount also delivered higher revenues and operating results in both its motion picture and television operations, he said.
Paramount's third quarter gains reflect increased feature motion picture sales to television networks and a rise in cable and syndication revenues of the television programming library, Viacom said.
Paramount results were boosted by the box office popularity of the recent films "Mission Impossible," "The First Wives Club," and "Primal Fear."
Viacom said its MTV Networks third quarter revenues of $349 million increased by 27 percent, mostly from double-digit gains in affiliate fees and advertising sales.
Redstone Thursday had accused Seagram Co. Ltd. Chief Executive Edgar Bronfman Jr. of trying to disrupt the companies' joint venture cable partnership by taking legal action against Viacom.

In his second day on the witness stand in Delaware Chancery Court, Redstone said Bronfman had assured him in March that Seagram would not sue Viacom over the launch of Viacom's new cable channel "Nick at Nite TV Land."
Canadian beverage firm Seagram filed suit in April, however, prompting Redstone to accuse Bronfman of trying to destroy the companies' USA Networks venture.
Viacom and Seagram, which also owns entertainment and theme park concern MCA Inc., have been fighting for control of the cable partership.
Viacom stock was up $1.625 at $34.25 in early afternoon trading on the American Stock Exchange.
